plan.summary: This 1-4 block is an off-camp build for boxing with a balanced strength, power, and endurance focus using bodyweight-only training. Week 1 establishes baseline performance on the main primary movements so later progress is clearer, then Weeks 2-3 build volume and control, and Week 4 trims fatigue with a deload while keeping speed and quality high. The full 12-week parent cycle will keep building force and work capacity first, then intensify, then shift toward sharper sport-relevant output.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general full-body strength, basic power, and repeatable conditioning with simple bodyweight methods that recover well alongside boxing.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress unilateral strength, explosive output, and aerobic power while keeping total fatigue manageable.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Turn the earlier work into faster, sharper bodyweight power and boxing-specific conditioning without forcing a speed peak.

exercises.name: 1a. Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high as you can and land quietly. Reset between reps so every jump stays crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space is tight. Start from a still quarter squat and explode up.

exercises.name: 1b. Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use strict bodyweight reps with full control. Stop one rep before form breaks and log reps on both sides. This sets your baseline for the next block.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up with easy split squat reps, then perform one hard bodyweight set per side with clean form and stop just before technique breaks. Log reps on each leg to establish your baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track your best strict rep count per side.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if regular split squats are too easy and you can keep balance and depth.

exercises.name: 2a. Push-Up
exercises.notes: Use a variation you can control cleanly. Keep ribs down, body straight, and press fast without losing position.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use hands on a bench, table, or sturdy surface if floor reps are not yet clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Knee Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need an easier option and keep full-body tension.

exercises.name: 2b. Towel Row Isometric
exercises.notes: Loop a towel around a sturdy post if available and pull hard with shoulders down. If no anchor is available, do prone back widows instead.

substitutionOptions.name: Back Widow
substitutionOptions.notes: Lie on the floor and drive elbows down to lift the upper back.

exercises.name: 3. Reverse Crunch
exercises.notes: Curl the pelvis up, move slowly, and keep the lower back controlled on the way down.

exercises.name: 4. Running Aerobic Intervals
exercises.notes: Build an aerobic base without turning this into a race.
